subject: Private deployment: egress stability, allowlist artefacts, and firewall requests
messages:
From: Aurora Health NetOps <netops@aurorahealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@partnercloud.io>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: stable egress IPs & allowlist for Redwood Private endpoint

Hi Olga,

We're onboarding Redwood Private into our staging VPC and the security team needs a concise set of artifacts to complete the allowlisting and firewall rule tickets. Specifically we need:
- A definitive list (CIDR / single IPs) to allow for outbound traffic from the runtime/control-plane to Redwood-managed services.
- Confirmation whether those IPs are static or short-lived, and if they rotate — frequency and rotation window.
- Port/FQDN expectations (ports, SNI/FQDN) so our perimeter inspection can be configured correctly.
- Any outbound dependencies (cloud provider endpoints, CDN, telemetry) that require additional entries.

Can you provide these as a short playbook + an allowlist CSV we can import into our firewall? We have a go-live compliance gate on Friday 2026-05-21, so a quick turnaround would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Marcus Hale
NetOps Lead — Aurora Health
netops@aurorahealth.com

--
Attachment: none in this thread yet
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Marcus Hale <netops@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@partnercloud.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:03:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: stable egress IPs & allowlist for Redwood Private endpoint

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up-front and then a short pack attached.

Summary answers:
- We can provide dedicated static egress IPs for the runtime lane in a single /32 per customer (control-plane endpoints differ — see note).
- Rotation: optional. If you elect static binding we reserve those IPs for your tenant; otherwise we operate ephemeral egress with a documented rotation window (24–72h).
- Required ports: 443 (TLS) outbound for runtime->model artifacts / health checks; 123/UDP only if you opt into NTP sync with Redwood; 853 for DNS-over-TLS if you enable outbound DoT.
- FQDN/SNI: runtime will contact model artifact hosting at artifacts.redwood-inference.com, telemetry at telemetry.redwood-inference.com, control plane at cp.redwood-inference.com. SNI inspection will see these hostnames inside TLS for some flows.

I've attached a redwood-allowlist-template.csv plus a short network-egress-design.pdf with the architecture and control-plane vs runtime distinctions. Marissa is sharing a proposed canonical rule set in a follow-up email.

One clarification request: do you need a signed attestation for SOC2 / perimeter audit, or just an importable list for your perimeter appliance? We can provide both, but the attestation takes a day to prepare.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-allowlist-template.csv, network-egress-design.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Marcus Hale <netops@aurorahealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 13:47:35 -07:00
Subject: Proposed firewall rules + definitive egress IPs (detailed)

Marcus — attaching concrete proposed rules you can import. Key points (expanded):

1) Egress IPs (runtime lane, dedicated-binding option)
- 18.142.91.203/32 (runtime egress - primary static IP)
- 18.142.91.204/32 (runtime egress - standby static IP, used for short failover)
- 34.201.7.120/32 (control-plane API endpoints - always allowed from management subnets)

Note: If you choose the "ephemeral" option we will not reserve 18.142.91.203 but instead provide our rotation policy (next section).

2) Rotation policy (ephemeral mode)
- Rotation window: typically 24–72 hours for individual egress addresses.
- Announcement: we publish rotation events to a dedicated status RSS and a push to the configured webhook.
- Exception: customers with UDR/allowlist constraints can request a one-time static binding; this requires a 48 hour provisioning window.

3) Ports and FQDNs
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to artifacts.redwood-inference.com (TLS; SNI will be present).
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com and cp.redwood-inference.com
- Optional: TCP/443 to registry.quant.redwood-inference.com for on-demand quantized model pulling (only if you opt into local-cache updates).
- No inbound openings required. All traffic is outbound-initiated from your private endpoint.

4) Firewall rule examples (for import)
- NAME: RW Runtime Egress - Primary
  SRC: 10.8.32.0/24 (your runtime subnet) -> DST: 18.142.91.203/32 TCP 443
- NAME: RW Controlplane API
  SRC: 10.8.64.0/28 (management) -> DST: 34.201.7.120/32 TCP 443
- NAME: RW Telemetry No-Inspect (optional)
  SRC: 10.8.32.0/24 -> DST: telemetry.redwood-inference.com TCP 443 (if you allow SNI-inspection bypass)

5) Perimeter inspection notes
- If you require TLS interception, provide a shortlist of hostnames and we can provide certificate pinning fingerprints for artifact downloads to ease inspection policies.
- For IDS/IPS correlation we recommend allowing IP->FQDN mapping for a 7 day retention window to avoid false positives during failovers.

6) Evidence for audit / SOC2
- Attached is a one-page extract we can sign off on for the allowlist (will include the static-binding timestamp and IPs). For a full SOC2 artifact we will need your Audit contact and 24–48 hours to populate the bundle.

Attachments referenced: eg egress-ip-rotation-policy.md (detailed rotation), redwood-allowlist-template.csv (CSV ready for import).

Let me know if you want us to open a short-lived VPN tunnel during your first acceptance test — speeds up traffic validation without touching firewall rules.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: egres-ip-rotation-policy.md (full policy), redwood-allowlist-template.csv
From: Marcus Hale <netops@aurorahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: CloudOps Partner <cloudops@partnercloud.io>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed firewall rules + definitive egress IPs (detailed)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before we import: 
1) Can you confirm SLAs on static-binding? If we request the reserved /32 for our tenant, is there an SLA for connectivity to that address (latency, availability)?
2) For the standby 18.142.91.204 — will there be an automatic failover window and DNS TTL we should model?
3) Please upload the signed one-page attestation to the HubSpot deal or share the DocuSign link — our audit team insists on a signed artifact in the ticket.

If those are OK we'll import the CSV and run the acceptance smoke tests tomorrow morning. Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

—Marcus
